citation: Bozhilova, Michelini, Kuntsi & Asherson. Mind wandering perspective on ADHD
main_result: Excessive spontaneous mind-wandering proposed as core mechanism of ADHD symptoms; deficient context regulation and sensory decoupling
relevance: Mechanism: justifies mind-wandering probes as a primary outcome

citation: Kofler, Spiegel, Soto, Irwin, Wells & Austin. Do working memory deficits underlie reading problems in ADHD?
design: dual-task experiment, controls for decoding and comorbid RD
main_result: WM load reduced comprehension in both groups, more in ADHD; did not slow reading speed; WM overlapped 41% of comprehension gap (exploratory)
relevance: Mechanism: working memory load, supports chunking and central-idea emphasis

citation: Parks, Moreau et al. The task matters: a scoping review on reading comprehension abilities in ADHD
main_result: Deficit size varies with task demands; most apparent on recall of central ideas
relevance: Outcome design: use central-idea recall, not short multiple choice

citation: Stern & Shalev. The role of sustained attention and text's conditions in reading comprehension among adolescents with ADHD and without it
manipulation_or_factor: spacing (standard vs spaced), medium (print vs screen)
main_result: Group differences in comprehension; presentation x spacing x sustained-attention interaction
relevance: Closest existing study to ours: presentation conditions x attention level

citation: Stern, Kolodny, Tsafrir, Cohen & Shalev. Unique patterns of eye movements characterizing inattentive reading in ADHD
outcome_measures: reading time, re-reading, first-pass word-length sensitivity
main_result: ADHD: longer reading time, far more words re-read 2+ times, first pass less sensitive to word length
relevance: Metric: re-reading count as unobtrusive attention-lapse signal; candidate model target

citation: Ben-Yehudah & Brann. Pay attention to digital text: media effects on comprehension and self-monitoring in higher-education students with ADHD
main_result: ADHD readers worse and overconfident on screen, matched controls on paper; self-highlighting helped only in print
relevance: Digital reading is where the ADHD gap appears; self-monitoring support matters

citation: Santos & Albuquerque. Effect of words highlighting in school tasks upon typical ADHD behaviors
main_result: Fewer inattentive behaviours and more correct answers with highlighting
relevance: Only ADHD-specific highlighting evidence; tiny n, good gap for us

citation: Rello, Saggion & Baeza-Yates. Keyword highlighting improves comprehension for people with dyslexia
main_result: Bolding main ideas improved comprehension for dyslexic readers
relevance: Method template for a keyword-highlighting condition

citation: Chen, Hung & Jian. Effects of text-to-speech on reading comprehension in junior high students with reading disabilities: an eye-tracking study
population: ADHD-related RD vs dyslexia vs typical
design: within-subject eye tracking, TTS vs silent
main_result: TTS improved comprehension for ADHD-related difficulties but not dyslexia; typical readers gained nothing
relevance: Strongest ADHD-specific presentation evidence; TTS as a condition

citation: Franklin, Mrazek, Anderson, Johnston, Smallwood, Kingstone & Schooler. Tracking distraction: mind-wandering, meta-awareness and ADHD symptomatology
main_result: ADHD symptoms linked to detrimental mind-wandering; meta-awareness mediates
relevance: Supports re-engagement prompts that raise meta-awareness; not reading-specific

verification: DOI NOT seen - verify before citing
citation: Brann & Sidi. Metacognitive scaffolding for digital reading and mind wandering
design: randomised, control vs scaffolding, long expository digital text
main_result: Scaffolding eliminated the ADHD comprehension gap; state mind-wandering explained the gap in control only
relevance: Most important intervention paper for us: attention re-engagement works; sample sizes conflict between versions

citation: Niklaus, Cai, Bylinskii & Wallace. Digital reading rulers
main_result: Three rulers improved dyslexic speed by 12-19 wpm; no ruler preferred by all; reasons: keep place, focus
relevance: Personalisation beats presets; crowdsourced design is accepted at CHI

citation: Llana, Baron, Yu, Hosseinpour, Suhail, Chin, Khadka & Wallace. Reading with diversity in mind: pupillometry and typography towards inclusive design for ADHD readers
design: in-lab eye tracking + pupillometry, 4 fonts x 3 sizes, quizzes, interviews
main_result: ADHD readers read faster with fewer saccades; speed-comprehension trade-off; interviews favour chunked distraction-free customisable interfaces
relevance: Only direct HCI ADHD reading study; shows speed is a misleading outcome

citation: Lee, Lee, Jung & Ames. Too long to read? Restructuring LLM responses for users with attention-related challenges
manipulation_or_factor: content condensation, visual hierarchy, original/adapted toggle
relevance: Closest system to ours; shows the gap: no controlled test

citation: Spiel, Hornecker, Williams & Good. ADHD and technology research - investigated by neurodivergent readers
main_result: Most ADHD tech aims to mitigate traits; little co-design; deficit framing resisted by participants
relevance: Framing and ethics: co-design, support not correction; reviewers at CHI/ASSETS expect this

citation: Rello & Baeza-Yates. How to present more readable text for people with dyslexia
venue: Universal Access in the Information Society 16(1):29-49
manipulation_or_factor: font size, colour, column width, character/line/paragraph spacing
main_result: Larger text and larger character spacing sped up both groups
relevance: Design template: how to run a multi-parameter presentation study

citation: Snell. No, Bionic Reading does not work
main_result: No difference in reading times; no advantage for fast or slow readers
relevance: Model of a clean null result; what to avoid testing
